title: Two Ways to Build a World · Why read this book?
description: Domination and partnership are recurrent coordination equilibria; technology and institutions change their relative cost without abolishing either repertoire.

readerInvitation.reasonToExist: A nearly forty-year-old idea claims societies keep organizing around partnership or domination. Two Ways to Build a World keeps Riane Eisler's contrast and drops the peaceful golden age. It treats domination and partnership as two recurring ways people coordinate under power.
readerInvitation.readerPromise: Domination and partnership are recurrent coordination equilibria; technology and institutions change their relative cost without abolishing either repertoire.
readerInvitation.audienceFit: readers interested in power, cooperation, institutional design, and how AI may reshape who can coordinate whom
readerInvitation.closingInvitation: Start with Chapter 3, From Binary to Coordinate System, and learn to map who holds power.
readerOutcomes: Instead of labelling whole civilizations, the book measures relationships along distinct dimensions.
It asks who can leave, speak, appeal, observe decisions, and impose sanctions.
Domination appears when wealth, media, office, and force convert into each other until escape disappears.

contentSamples.readingValue: Hierarchy can stay legitimate when its purpose, scope, duration, review, and exit are clear.
